subject: math
title: Practice: subtracting from a negative number
instructions: Work every problem on paper first. Then type your answer and press Check. You get two tries on each question. Type each answer as a number, and type a negative number with the minus sign, like −1.

skills.int-sign: Sign of an answer with negatives

sections.name: Part A: Warm-up
sections.desc: Start above 0 and take away more: count down to 0, then keep going.

items.q: Warm up. Each one starts above 0 and takes away more than it has.
items.hint: Count down to 0 first, then keep going below 0 for what is left.

items.q: Find each value.
items.hint: Start at the first number on a number line and move left.

sections.name: Part B: A negative minus a positive
sections.desc: Below 0, minus moves you farther down. Add the sizes, keep the minus sign.

items.q: Look at −5 − 4.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Before you work it out: will the answer be positive, negative, or zero?

a: −5 is left of 0. Subtracting 4 moves 4 more to the left, so the answer is negative.
Add the sizes: 5 + 4 = 9. Keep the minus sign.
items.hint: You start below 0 and move farther down. Can you ever get back up to 0 that way?

items.q: Look at −3 − 8.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Before you work it out: will the answer be positive, negative, or zero?

a: −3 is left of 0. Subtracting 8 moves 8 more to the left, so the answer is negative.
Add the sizes: 3 + 8 = 11. Keep the minus sign.
items.hint: You start below 0 and move farther down. Can you ever get back up to 0 that way?

items.q: Find the value.
a: Start at −6 and move 6 more to the left.
items.hint: Both numbers have size 6. You are moving away from 0, not toward it.

items.q: Sign first, then the size. Find each value.
items.hint: Each one starts below 0 and moves farther left. Add the two sizes and keep the minus sign.

items.q: Bigger numbers, same rule. Find each value.
items.hint: Add the two sizes. The answer is below 0.

items.q: Which way gives the right value of −7 − 5?

options: Subtract 5 from 7, then make the answer negative
Add 7 and 5, then make the answer negative

a: −7 is 7 below 0. Subtracting 5 moves 5 more below 0.
Answer: add 7 and 5, then make the answer negative
items.hint: Picture it on a number line. Do you end up 2 below 0 or 12 below 0?

items.q: Sam says −9 − 4 = −5.
a: Sam found 9 − 4 = 5, which is the distance between the sizes.
But −9 − 4 starts 9 below 0 and moves 4 more down: 9 + 4 = 13 below 0.
Answers: a) he subtracted the sizes, b) −13
items.hint: Is −5 closer to 0 or farther from 0 than −9? Subtracting should take you farther.

items.q: Ava says −6 − 8 = 14.
a: But the answer is 14 below 0, so it needs the minus sign.
Answers: a) she dropped the minus sign, b) −14
items.hint: Where did she start, above 0 or below 0? Which way did she move?

learn.title: Below zero, minus takes you farther down
where: Thermometers, elevation maps and parking floors all go below zero. When the temperature is already below zero and it drops, it gets colder, never warmer.
The same is true for every number below zero: subtracting moves you left, away from 0.

steps.text: Two ways to slip: subtracting the sizes, or dropping the minus sign. Check every answer: did you end up farther from 0, and below it?

example.q: On a winter night in Alaska the temperature is −19°F. By morning it has dropped 6 more degrees. What is the temperature in the morning?
steps: It starts below 0 and drops, so the answer is negative.

sections.name: Part C: Mixed signs
sections.desc: Decide the sign first: where do you start, and which way do you move?

items.q: Same numbers, different signs. Decide the sign of each answer first.
items.hint: Plus moves right, minus moves left. Where does each one start?

items.q: Decide the sign first, then find each value.
items.hint: For a), you start at −10 and move only 3 to the right. Do you reach 0?

items.q: Find each value.
items.hint: For a), you start below 0 and move farther left. For c), you start at 15 and take away more than you have.

items.q: Which is less: −8 − 3 or −8 + 3?
a: −11 is farther left on the number line, so it is less.
items.hint: Work out both. On a number line, the number farther left is less.

items.q: Find the missing number.
a: a) From −5 to −12 is 7 more to the left, so ? = 7.
b) Moving 6 left lands on −10, so the start is 6 to the right of −10, which is −4.
items.hint: Draw a number line. How far apart are the two numbers you know?

sections.name: Part D: Word problems
sections.desc: Drops, dives, falls and lowers mean subtract. Rises and raises mean add.

items.q: At 6 in the morning the temperature was −3°F. By midnight it had dropped 9 degrees. What was the temperature at midnight?

parts.prompt: Temperature at midnight (type it as a number)

items.hint: It was already below 0. Does dropping make it colder or warmer?

items.q: A submarine is at −40 meters, which means 40 meters below the surface. It dives down 25 more meters. Where is it now?

parts.prompt: Its position now (type it as a number)

items.hint: Going down from below the surface takes it farther below.

items.q: In a tall building, the ground floor is floor 0 and the parking floors below it are −1, −2, −3, and so on. An elevator is on floor −2.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: It goes down 3 floors. Which floor is it on now?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: From there it goes up 9 floors. Which floor is it on now?

items.hint: Down means subtract and up means add. Picture the floors as a number line standing up.

items.q: A lake is 6 inches below its normal level, so its level is −6 inches.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A dry month lowers it 4 more inches. What is its level now?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Then rain raises it 7 inches. What is its level now?

items.hint: Lowers means subtract, raises means add. For b), 7 inches up is not enough to get back to 0.

items.q: At noon the temperature was 5°C. It fell 8 degrees by evening, then fell 6 more degrees overnight.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What was the temperature in the evening?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: What was the temperature by morning?

items.hint: For b), start from your answer to a). It was already below 0 and it kept falling.

sections.name: Part E: Stretch
sections.desc: Longer chains. One step at a time.

items.q: Work from left to right. Find each value.
items.hint: One step at a time. After the first step, you are subtracting from a negative number.

items.q: Use the order of operations. Find each value.
items.hint: Multiply or find the power first. Then subtract, using what you know about going below 0.

items.q: Start at 0 and keep subtracting 7: 0, −7, −14, and so on. 0 is the 1st number in the list. What is the 10th number?
a: From the 1st number to the 10th number there are 9 steps of 7.
items.hint: Count the steps between the 1st number and the 10th, not the numbers themselves.

items.q: A diver goes from −12 meters to −30 meters. How far down did she go? Type the distance in meters.
a: From −12 down to −30: how many steps left on the number line?
items.hint: Both numbers are below 0. How far apart are they on the number line?

note: Sign first, then the size. A negative number minus a positive number is always negative: add the two sizes and keep the minus sign.
